expectedText: Week Two of the Rock & Road tour: seven days on the pocketed limestone that birthed modern sport climbing — where Wolfgang Güllich pulled monos and Kurt Albert invented the redpoint.
You can hang on forever but crimping through a mono has you humbled. Frankenjura's short, bouldery routes will fix that fast — and painfully.
You've watched the old Güllich footage more times than you'd admit. This is the actual rock. Come touch the holds that made sport climbing what it is.
You want Europe's best rock without Europe's worst trip-planning admin. We've handled the logistics for eight weeks straight — you just show up and climb.

Frankenjura is the birthplace of modern sport climbing — the rock where Wolfgang Güllich pioneered Action Directe and Kurt Albert invented the entire concept of the redpoint. Your fingers are about to owe this place an apology.

10,000+ routes spread across 1,000 crags of pocketed, powerful limestone. Mono pulls, full-hand jugs, and everything sharp in between — this is where climbers come to build the finger strength their egos have been writing checks for.
Seven days of pocket-pulling by day, traditional Bavarian beer gardens by night. Come for the climbing history, stay for the schnitzel.
This leg is one stop on an 8-week circuit across Europe. Book just this week, or grab the full tour and follow the sun (and the sends) from Bohemia all the way to Spain.
No stock photos, no staged sends — just climbers earning it on the same limestone that made climbing history.
Maximum climbing time, minimum logistical hassle. Coaching happens on the rock, not in a classroom.
One week gets you the pocket-pulling initiation. Eight weeks gets you the entire European climbing continent — and a road-trip family you didn't know you needed.

Spaces fill fast, and we only run this leg with a minimum of 3 climbers. Secure your spot now — or drop us a line first if you've got questions.

Rising out of lush Bavarian forests, Frankenjura's white and grey limestone formations are climbing's most storied proving ground — over 10,000 routes across 1,000 crags, most of them vertical-to-overhanging walls riddled with pockets of every size.

This is where the redpoint was invented and where finger strength gets built the hard way. Expect technical face climbing, powerful pocket pulls, and a level of route-setting history you can't find anywhere else.
Basic shared accommodation arranged with local climbing hosts — hostel or campsite bungalows with bunk beds, and a short drive from the crag.
Fly into Nuremberg. Local transport is organised via shared rental cars once you land — no navigating unfamiliar Autobahns solo.
All safety equipment provided — ropes, draws, helmets, slings. Bring your own shoes and harness if you have preferences; we've got spares if you don't.
Minimum 3 climbers to run the trip. Small enough for real coaching, never a crowd-control exercise.

Not included: local transport within the destination and travel & climbing insurance. Dinners are flexible — some nights the group cooks together as a bit of built-in team-building, other nights everyone heads out to a local spot for a reasonable price. It comes down to the group's dynamic, energy, and what everyone feels like doing.
What level do I need to be?
You should be comfortable leading 6b indoors or 6a outdoors. Frankenjura rewards finger strength and technical footwork — if you're strong on pockets or want to be, you'll fit right in.
Do I need my own gear?
Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide all safety equipment — ropes, draws, helmets, slings — plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, and yes, a sleeping bag).
Food arrangements and any included meals are confirmed before departure.
What if fewer than 3 people book?
We need a minimum of 3 participants to run this leg. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative trip, or a full refund. No hard feelings.
Can I join more than one week of the tour?
Absolutely — that's the whole idea. Book the full 8-week Rock & Road Tour at the current full-tour price and follow the sun (and the sends) across eight destinations.
Where do I fly in and out of?
Nuremberg Airport, for both arrival and departure.
[Design preview] Carmen M. Rock & Road · Tour Alum

One past Rock & Road climber credits Jan and the crew with pushing her far beyond what she thought her limits were — and with turning a summer spent climbing across Europe into one of the most meaningful experiences of her life.
I'd never climbed on pockets before Frankenjura. By day three my forearms had filed a formal complaint. By day seven I was onsighting things I'd have laughed at a week earlier.
Standing where Güllich climbed Action Directe was worth the trip on its own. Getting proper coaching on pocket technique while I was there was the bonus I didn't expect.

Rockbusters' founder and head coach, with 25+ years on rock. Jan traded a career in social work for a life of pushing climbers past their limits — technically and mentally — and hasn't looked back since.

A former World Cup podium finisher and lifelong onsight addict, Klemen brings decades of high-level competition experience to the mental side of climbing — fear management, focus, and taking a big fall without flinching.
Part of the crew across every leg of the Rock & Road tour, Linda knows how to read pocketed limestone as well as sandstone — and exactly which route will teach you the most without breaking you.
Local knowledge is everything on unfamiliar rock, and Zbyněk has it in spades — from the classic Frankenjura testpieces to the quiet crags the guidebooks skip.

expectedText: Week Seven of the Rock & Road tour: seven days on Catalonia's otherworldly conglomerate walls, where pockets range from shallow monos to entire-hand jugs, and gravity is apparently more of a suggestion.
You've spent the tour perfecting technique, footwork, and patience. Margalef doesn't care about any of that as much as it cares whether your fingers can close around a cobblestone.
Sandstone, pockets, granite, tufas, limestone crimps — you've done six kinds of rock already. Conglomerate is the one everyone talks about and nobody quite believes until they touch it.
You want Europe's best rock without Europe's worst trip-planning admin. We've handled the logistics for eight weeks straight — you just show up and climb.

Margalef's conglomerate rock is unlike anything else on the tour — a matrix of rounded cobbles set in cement-like stone, studded across walls that genuinely look like they shouldn't hold weight. They do. Mostly.

This is pocket pulling in its most extreme form: shallow monos that barely accept a fingertip, deep three-finger holes that count as a rest. The deep red and orange walls rise from olive groves and pine forest, with the occasional hermitage wedged impossibly into the cliff.
Seven days climbing in a distinctly Catalan atmosphere — passionate, proud, and just as obsessed with the send as you are — evenings spent recovering by the reservoir and eating well in the village.
This leg is one stop on an 8-week circuit across Europe. Book just this week, or grab the full tour and follow the sun (and the sends) from Bohemia all the way to Spain.
No stock photos, no staged sends — just climbers pulling on rock that shouldn't work but somehow does.

The Catalan climbing scene here is passionate and progressive, pushing difficulty on these unique walls year-round thanks to a microclimate that allows both sun and shade sectors to stay in condition.

children.text: Oltre Finale — literally "beyond Finale" — is the tour's best-kept secret. Tucked into the "Valley of the Rock" past the crowds of Finale Ligure proper, this is where 2,000+ routes of compact limestone sit quietly waiting for people willing to drive a little further.

Expect a bit of everything: technical crimps, perfect pockets, the occasional tufa, and faces ranging from delicate slabs to genuinely rude overhangs. Creative movement isn't optional here — it's the whole curriculum.
Seven days climbing sun-warmed limestone by day, cooling off in mountain streams and eating your way through Ligurian villages by night — where the espresso is strong and nobody's in a hurry.

expectedText: Week Three of the Rock & Road tour: seven days on Austrian granite, where crystal friction replaces bolts and pockets, slab footwork replaces raw power, and alpine air replaces your gym-conditioned lungs.
Frankenjura left your forearms wrecked and your footwork rusty. Zillertal's granite slabs will gently remind you that climbing is also, occasionally, about your feet.
You climb partly for the send and partly for the view. Alpine meadows, glacier-fed streams, and mountain huts deliver both in equal, unreasonable measure.
You want Europe's best rock without Europe's worst trip-planning admin. We've handled the logistics for eight weeks straight — you just show up and climb.

Zillertal is the tour's reset button. After sandstone ethics and pocket-pulling power, Austria hands you clean granite slabs, crystal edges, and a whole new relationship with trusting your feet.
This is technical footwork country — thin smears, positive crimps that feel hand-carved, and exposure dramatic enough that you'll actually look at the view instead of just your chalk bag.
Seven days climbing surrounded by alpine meadows and mountain huts, evenings spent recovering in glacier-fed streams and demolishing Tyrolean dumplings in village cafés.
No stock photos, no staged sends — just climbers trusting their feet on Austria's finest granite.
Maximum climbing time, minimum logistical hassle. Coaching happens on the rock, not in a classroom.
One week gets you the granite initiation. Eight weeks gets you the entire European climbing continent — and a road-trip family you didn't know you needed.
Spaces fill fast, and we only run this leg with a minimum of 3 climbers. Secure your spot now — or drop us a line first if you've got questions.

Pristine granite walls rise dramatically against Austria's most stunning alpine scenery. Rough, crystal-featured rock offers incredible friction and a completely different climbing style from anything else on the tour — slabs, cracks, and edges that feel sculpted for climbers' hands.

Home to the famous Ewige Jagdgründe crag and a valley full of hidden bouldering circuits, Zillertal's microclimate lets us chase perfect sending conditions across elevations, whatever the weather does.
Basic shared accommodation arranged with local climbing hosts — hostel or campsite bungalows with bunk beds, tucked into the valley.
Fly into Munich. Local transport is organised via shared rental cars or shuttles once you land — no navigating Alpine passes solo.
All safety equipment provided — ropes, draws, helmets, slings. Bring your own shoes and harness if you have preferences; we've got spares if you don't.
Minimum 3 climbers to run the trip. Small enough for real coaching, never a crowd-control exercise.

Not included: local transport within the destination, travel & climbing insurance, and food. Optional communal dinner arrangements and prices are confirmed before departure.
What level do I need to be?

You should be comfortable leading 6b indoors or 6a outdoors. Zillertal rewards technical footwork and trust over raw power — if you're strong but new to slab and friction climbing, you'll fit right in.
Do I need my own gear?
Bring climbing shoes and a harness you trust. We provide all safety equipment — ropes, draws, helmets, slings — plus a full kit list once you book (down jacket, headlamp, and yes, a sleeping bag).
Food arrangements and any included meals are confirmed before departure.
What if fewer than 3 people book?
We need a minimum of 3 participants to run this leg. If numbers don't add up, we'll offer an equivalent (or better) alternative trip, or a full refund. No hard feelings.
Can I join more than one week of the tour?
Absolutely — that's the whole idea. Book the full 8-week Rock & Road Tour at the current full-tour price and follow the sun (and the sends) across eight destinations.
Where do I fly in and out of?
Munich International Airport, for both arrival and departure.
